definitions.meaning: tackle is gear or equipment, as in fishing tackle
the party machine, the structure of officials that runs a political body

explanation.definitionFit: Equipment is called tackle, and the administrative machine of a party or state is its organisational structure.

clue.text: Parcel containing a ring turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for ring is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to toll is to ring a bell

explanation.surface: A package with a ring inside, found upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parcel' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in parcel out. 'turned up' reverses TOLL to LLOT, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To parcel out is to distribute or share, giving each a portion.

clue.text: Heaving silver up found on Eastern wreck…

indicators.note: heaving suggests the letters being tossed about and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Treasure hauled up from the sea bed on a wreck in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaving' rearranges SILVERUP into PULVERIS, and E is added. 'wreck' looks like the noun of the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulverise something is to smash it to powder, destroying it utterly.

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the two words wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: A pot found among the rocks at an archaeological site on Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges PLACE and CRETE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle is any container, and vessel is a general word for such a holder.

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: thirty is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: A dull personality who strictly observes the day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' places S inside THIRTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry in the sense of parched means wanting a drink.

indicators.note: outwardly says the abbreviation for stone lies on the outside, around the other word

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for the stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds
alien means strange or foreign

explanation.surface: An odd rock bearing marks on its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' wraps ST around ALIEN. A stone is a British unit of weight (14 lb), abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is prominent or conspicuous, standing out clearly.

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the numeral goes into the other word

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does save
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty people going into a pub to be consoled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts L inside SAVE. 'bar' looks like a pub but means 'except'.
explanation.definitionFit: A balm or ointment soothes, and figuratively anything that consoles is called this.

indicators.note: the coach has lost a letter, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: a stage is a stagecoach; the 's stands for has

explanation.surface: A rookie coach has wasted time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach's' is 'coach has'; a stagecoach is a STAGE, and 'lost' removes T. 'Green' looks like inexperienced but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a greyish-green colour, named after the herb's leaves.

indicators.note: acquires means takes in, so the abbreviation goes inside the currency

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy, foreign money to a British solver

explanation.surface: Overseas money gains a British endorsement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquires' puts B inside LIRA.
explanation.definitionFit: The scales are one of the twelve zodiac signs.

clue.text: That's just typical of a model!

definitions.text: That's just typical of a model!

parts.words: That's just typical of a model!
parts.note: read as a complaint about a fashion model's behaviour, but it means serving as a perfect pattern or example

explanation.surface: A grumble about a catwalk star behaving true to type.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both 'serving as a typical example' and 'worthy to be a model', so the clue's 'typical' and 'model' both define it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serving as a perfect pattern or specimen is worthy of imitation, like a model.

clue.text: Shrub, the European kind, in season almost

indicators.note: in places the Italian article inside the shortened word
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to lace a drink is to season or flavour it with spirits
il is the European (Italian) kind of the word the

explanation.surface: A European variety of bush that is nearly in season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the European kind' is a foreign form of 'the', here Italian IL. 'almost' cuts LACE to LAC, and 'in' puts IL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blossom.

parts.note: reads as mysterious people, but the characters are letters of handwriting that cannot be read

explanation.surface: Describing enigmatic people who give nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inscrutable' suggests unreadable faces; 'characters' are written letters that cannot be made out.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing whose letters cannot be deciphered is unreadable.

clue.text: Breaks in, locating spring in more than one lock

indicators.note: in places the word for spring inside the locks of hair

parts.note: locks of hair are tresses
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks in by finding the spring in several locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' and 'spring' suggest a door mechanism, but the locks are hair and the spring is a SPA, which goes inside TRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: To go onto someone's property without permission is to intrude, breaking in.

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the letter for river goes inside

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: A river fish makes better eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts R inside CAP. 'Better' looks like an adjective but is the verb 'outdo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish of ponds and rivers, often bred in ponds.

clue.text: Like a unit operating with batteries?

definitions.text: Like a unit operating with batteries?

parts.words: Like a unit operating with batteries?
parts.note: suggests an electrical device run on cells, but the unit is a military body and batteries are groups of artillery guns

explanation.surface: Describing a gadget that runs on cells.
explanation.walkthrough: A battery is an artillery unit, so the 'unit' is an army regiment, not a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to an army regiment, a military unit that may include artillery batteries.

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
a means one, as in a single thing
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: The first person standing in a formal queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run in order, with A sitting 'in' the gap between PRIM and RY; RY for railway line is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something primary is chief or earliest in order.

indicators.note: carved means cut into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A panda figure carved from a piece of coral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved' rearranges PART and CORAL. A Panda car was a British police patrol car, once painted blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda car was the British nickname for a police vehicle on the beat.

clue.text: Soothing word's given to a girl

parts.note: there is said to soothe, as in 'there, there'; with the 's attached

explanation.surface: A comforting word is offered to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' is said to comfort someone ('there, there'), and 'word's' keeps its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female given name.

parts.note: suggests customs declarations, but means pronouncing someone free of an obligation or blame, from the Latin for burden

explanation.surface: Telling customs officers you have nothing to pay on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declare' and 'duty-free' evoke customs, but the word means to release from a burden (Latin onus) or clear of blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to free them from blame or an obligation.

indicators.note: creaky suggests something rickety and out of true, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh noise coming from squeaky boat tillers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creaky' rearranges TILLERS. 'Grating' looks like a harsh sound but is a lattice.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework of crossed strips, like a lattice for climbing plants.

clue.text: Second, and one to advance? Unlikely

parts.note: a lender advances money

explanation.surface: Asking a second backer to front cash seems a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' means lend money. 'Unlikely' defines it as in 'a slender chance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slim chance is a small one, so the outcome is improbable.

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the two pieces go inside the word for crack

parts.note: to have a crack at something is to have a try
a log is a record; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A band member puts their record into a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record's' is 'record is'. 'into' puts I and LOG inside TRY ('have a crack').
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three related works forms a group of books or films.

clue.text: Great Italian cast in bronze, I see

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the two letters for Italian are tossed into the other order

parts.note: a tan is a bronzed skin colour
C sounds like see, a standard crossword abbreviation

explanation.surface: A celebrated Italian sculpture cast in bronze, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' turns IT into TI. 'cast in bronze' looks like a sculpture but the words split: TAN for 'bronze', then I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanic means gigantic, like the Titans of myth.

clue.text: Company heading off for Northern river

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is cut away

parts.note: a house is a business firm, a company

explanation.surface: The company boss leaves for a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes H from HOUSE. The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire in the north of England.

indicators.note: mostly means all but the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: fly as an adjective means sharp or cunning, like shrewd

explanation.surface: Something that eats bugs, mostly flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect but is the adjective 'cunning'; 'mostly' drops the D of SHREWD.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a small mammal that feeds on insects.

definitions.meaning: a hamlet is a small village, with the 's standing for is
the resolution of a dispute or deal

explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a small community, and the resolution of a dispute is an agreed ending.

definitions.meaning: closed fast so nothing gets in, as in airtight

explanation.definitionFit: Something closed fast is secure, and something that grips closely is constricting.

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the chess pieces go around the letter

parts.note: castles are chessmen, so men
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A view of castles around Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts MEN, chess pieces such as castles, around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's bearing or expression is their look or air.

parts.note: Carrie is a girl's name
Don is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young woman meets a young man and they make eyes at each other.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry on with someone is to have a flirtation or affair.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry on means to dally or have an affair.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for essence

parts.note: a tang is a distinctive flavour, an essence

explanation.surface: A speech that is Western at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts W inside TANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive nasal manner of speaking, an accent.

clue.text: Stick end burnt off to pale ash

indicators.note: the end of the stick is burnt away, so its last letter is removed

parts.note: a rod is a stick
wan means pale

explanation.surface: A stick whose end is charred down to pale ash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end burnt off' cuts ROD to RO; WAN follows. 'ash' looks like cinders but is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is another name for this tree.

clue.text: Muse on or about a prayer

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a collect is a short prayer in Christian liturgy

explanation.surface: Pondering whether or not to say a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: A collect is a short liturgical prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, pondering it.
